cells.question: Q01

passages.quote: System Card: Claude Sonnet 4.5 September 2025
Changelog October 10, 2025

cells.note: The cover carries a month only. The changelog lists revisions dated October 10, 2025 and December 3, 2025; the copy read includes both.

cells.question: Q02

passages.quote: Informed by the testing described here, we have deployed Claude Sonnet 4.5 under the AI Safety Level 3 Standard.

cells.note: The card states that the model has been deployed, without a release date or release form. Third parties had pre-release access, one from September 22 (§7.3.1); that is a testing date, not a release date.

search.read: Whole-card term search (149 pages) and reading of the hits; Abstract, §1, §7.3, §9

setAside.reason: September 22 is the date of a pre-deployment snapshot’s access, not the model’s release.

cells.question: Q03

passages.quote: The Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP) evaluation process

cells.note: The text gives no edition. The link annotation on the policy’s name in §9.1 (PDF p. 125) targets the fixed RSP file whose cover reads “Version 2.2, Effective May 14, 2025”, the file targeted by Claude Haiku 4.5 and Claude Opus 4.6 (maintainer decision 4a). The links on the name on PDF pp. 9, 33 and 41 target an announcement, the undated policy page and the 2023 announcement.

crossFamily.result: material disagreement, applied: the checker reads stated (blind) under decision 4a, from the link annotation in §9.1, PDF p. 125, to the fixed RSP v2.2 file. The pack had read partly, having checked the annotations on PDF pp. 9, 33 and 41 but not this one. The preparer accepts the checker’s reading on rereading the annotations (pypdf, 2026-11-09).

cells.question: Q04

passages.locator: §5 Cyber capabilities, PDF p. 33 (link annotation on “Responsible Scaling”)
passages.quote: Responsible Scaling

cells.note: The words “Responsible Scaling” carry a hyperlink to https://anthropic.com/responsible-scaling-policy, the policy’s undated web page. Two other links on the policy name target announcement pages (PDF pp. 9 and 41).

cells.question: Q05

passages.quote: we have not determined whether Claude Sonnet 4.5 has definitively passed the capabilities threshold that requires ASL-3 protections. Rather, we cannot clearly rule out ASL-3 risks for Claude Sonnet 4.5.

cells.note: The card states that ASL-3 risks cannot be ruled out and that the model remained below the ASL-4 thresholds in all domains of concern (§1.2.4). The card states that the model did not meet the RSP’s criteria requiring a fuller assessment (§1.2.1).

cells.question: Q06

passages.quote: we are deploying Claude Sonnet 4.5 with ASL-3 measures as a precautionary, provisional action.
RSP safeguards applied to Claude Sonnet 4.5: ASL-3 Standard

cells.note: The card ties the ASL-3 Standard to the determination in Q05. A stated safeguard is the developer’s account.

cells.question: Q07

passages.quote: Demonstrated enhanced performance on several biological risk evaluations while remaining below ASL-4 rule-out thresholds

cells.note: Biological evaluations were automated. The card states that it runs no internal chemical evaluations for the RSP (§9.2.1) and no internal radiological or nuclear evaluations, which a partnership with the US NNSA covers without published results (§9.2.2).

cells.question: Q08

passages.quote: we believe that current AI models, including Claude Sonnet 4.5, do not yet possess the capabilities necessary to substantially increase the number or scale of cyber-enabled catastrophic events.

cells.note: The card states that the RSP sets no formal cyber threshold and that cyber needs ongoing assessment (§9.4).

cells.question: Q09

passages.quote: Exhibited improved autonomy capabilities in software engineering and AI research tasks, though still below the ASL-4 rule-out threshold.

cells.note: The card also states that some tasks in its first AI R&D suite are saturated and no longer valid as rule-out evaluations, and rests the conclusion on the second suite and an internal survey (§9.3.1.3).

cells.question: Q10

passages.quote: attempts to manipulate users toward certain views

cells.note: The card lists attempts to manipulate users toward certain views among the behaviours its alignment assessment looked for. No outcome specific to persuasion or manipulation was found; this is not a reported persuasion evaluation with people.

search.read: Whole-card term search (149 pages) and reading of the hits; Abstract, §1, §7.3, §9

setAside.reason: “Influence operations” is a domain of harmful-request testing (content safety), not an evaluation of the model’s persuasive capability.

cells.question: Q11

passages.quote: We saw roughly a 60% improvement on our primary misalignment metric over Claude Sonnet 4

cells.note: The card reports automated behavioural audits, deception, sabotage-capability and evaluation-awareness tests, interpretability investigations and third-party findings, with conclusions. Apollo Research’s findings say that low deception rates may be partly driven by evaluation awareness (§7.3.2).

crossFamily.result: minor, applied: the quotation stops before the developer’s characterisation of the earlier model. Status agrees.

cells.question: Q12

passages.locator: §4.2.1 Gray Swan Agent Red Teaming benchmark, PDF p. 29
passages.quote: One of our external red-teaming partners, Gray Swan, conducted their Agent Red Teaming (ART) benchmark

cells.note: Scope: prompt-injection attacks on agents in four categories, run against 23 models from Anthropic and other developers. The card states that the CBRN assessment for this model did not include external red teaming by experts (§9.2).

cells.question: Q13

passages.quote: We shared late pre-deployment snapshots of Claude Sonnet 4.5 with two organizations … the independent nonprofit Apollo Research.

cells.note: Apollo Research’s summary of findings is reproduced in §7.3.2. Gray Swan ran a prompt-injection benchmark on the model (§4.2.1).

cells.question: Q14

passages.quote: UK AISI was given access to [an early snapshot of Claude Sonnet 4.5] on September 22nd

cells.note: The UK AI Security Institute tested pre-deployment snapshots for misalignment-related propensities; its summary is reproduced in §7.3.1. A partnership with the US NNSA on nuclear and radiological evaluation of Anthropic’s models is described without results or a statement that this model was tested (§9.2.2).

cells.question: Q15

passages.quote: the process under which we decided to release it under the AI Safety Level 3 Standard.

cells.note: The developer, in its own voice, describes a decision to release the model under the ASL-3 Standard. The card adds that the ASL determination was overseen by the Responsible Scaling Officer (§1.2.3).

cells.question: Q16

passages.quote: our alignment evals may underestimate the model’s propensity to perform harmful actions in more realistic conditions.

cells.note: The card also states that some AI R&D tasks are saturated and no longer valid as rule-out evaluations (§9.3.1.3) and lists open questions on alignment assessment (§7.7).

passages.quote: System Card: Claude Haiku 4.5 October 2025

cells.question: Q02

passages.quote: Informed by the testing described here, we have deployed Claude Haiku 4.5 under the AI Safety Level 2 Standard

cells.note: The card states that the model has been deployed and refers to its launch post (§1), without a release date or release form.

search.read: Whole card (40 pages): Abstract, §1, §§2–6

cells.question: Q03

passages.quote: Anthropic’s Responsible Scaling Policy requires us to run evaluations to determine the AI Safety Level (ASL) Standard

cells.note: The edition is identified by link annotation (maintainer decision 4a): the policy’s name on PDF pp. 4 and 7 links to the RSP file whose cover reads Version 2.2, effective May 14, 2025.

cells.question: Q04

passages.locator: §1.2.1 Overview, PDF p. 7 (link annotation on the policy name)
passages.quote: see the Responsible Scaling Policy for details of what this Standard entails

cells.note: The policy’s name links to https://www-cdn.anthropic.com/872c653b2d0501d6ab44cf87f43e1dc4853e4d37.pdf (RSP v2.2).

cells.question: Q05

passages.quote: Our evaluations determined that Claude Haiku 4.5 met the ASL-3 rule-out threshold.

cells.note: The card states that the model remained well below ASL-3 thresholds in all domains of concern and is deployed under the ASL-2 Standard. The ASL-3 rule-out rests on automated biology and autonomy evaluations (§1.2.1, §6.1).

cells.question: Q06

passages.quote: RSP safeguards applied to Claude Haiku 4.5: AI Safety Level 2 (ASL-2) Standard

cells.note: The card ties the ASL-2 Standard to the ASL-3 rule-out in Q05. It names no individual ASL-2 measure in this passage. A stated safeguard is the developer’s account.

cells.question: Q07

passages.quote: Taken in aggregate, we consider these results to be sufficient to rule out the necessity of applying ASL-3 safeguards to Claude Haiku 4.5.

cells.note: Biological evaluations only, automated, with ASL-4 evaluations run as a precaution (§6.2.3.2); no chemical, radiological or nuclear results are reported.

cells.question: Q08

passages.quote: we ran a subset of our cyber evaluations on Claude Haiku 4.5.

cells.note: The card reports a subset of cyber challenge evaluations with results compared with Claude Sonnet 4, and states that the RSP sets no formal cyber threshold. No conclusion in threshold or risk terms was found for cyber.

setAside.reason: “well below ASL-3 thresholds across all domains of concern” is general; §6.4 states that the RSP has no formal cyber threshold.

cells.question: Q09

passages.quote: scoring very similarly to Claude Sonnet 4’s 15.4/42 (36.7%), and remaining below the 50% threshold.

cells.note: The autonomy evaluation is the ASL-3 checkpoint (hard subset of SWE-bench Verified); no AI R&D suite results are reported.

search.read: Whole card (40 pages): Abstract, §1, §§2–6

setAside.reason: “manipulate” concerns external prompt injection against the agent, not persuasion of people by the model.

cells.question: Q11

passages.locator: §4 Alignment and welfare assessments, PDF p. 21
passages.quote: Claude Haiku 4.5 showed safety properties similar to or stronger than Claude Sonnet 4.5 across the board on our tests for high-stakes forms of misalignment.

cells.note: The card reports automated behavioural audits (including user deception and self-preservation), an agentic misalignment suite whose full results it does not report because of evaluation awareness (§4.2), and sabotage-capability tests.

cells.question: Q12

passages.quote: using the same external red-teaming benchmark and suite of internal evaluations we used for

cells.note: Scope: prompt-injection attacks on agents (Gray Swan’s Agent Red Teaming benchmark, 25 model variants, §3.2.1). The RSP assessment included no expert red-teaming (§6.1).

cells.question: Q13

passages.locator: §3.2.1 Gray Swan Agent Red Teaming benchmark, PDF p. 17
passages.quote: Gray Swan conducted their Agent Red Teaming (ART) benchmark

cells.note: The card calls this a third-party, non-governmental evaluation of the model’s vulnerability to prompt injection (§6.5).

search.read: Whole card (40 pages): Abstract, §1, §§2–6

setAside.reason: States that pre-deployment evaluations with external government partners were not conducted for this model, which is not considered a frontier model.

cells.question: Q15

passages.quote: Informed by the testing described here, we have deployed Claude Haiku 4.5 under the AI Safety Level 2 Standard as described in our Responsible Scaling Policy.

cells.note: The card states the deployment as following from its testing; the section headed “Decision” (§1.2.2) states the ASL determination, not a decision to release, and names no maker.

search.read: Abstract, §1.2, §6

setAside.reason: States the ASL-3 rule-out determination, not a release decision.

cells.question: Q16

passages.quote: with 9% of transcripts showing clear signs of verbalized evaluation awareness of some kind. This does reduce our trust in our results to an extent.

cells.note: The card also states that the RSP assessment was automated only, without human uplift trials or expert red-teaming (§6.1).

passages.quote: as defined in our Responsible Scaling Policy (RSP)

cells.question: Q05

passages.quote: Our determination is that Claude Opus 4.6 does not cross either the AI R&D-4 or the CBRN-4 capability threshold.

cells.note: The card applies the ASL-3 Standard and repeats from the Claude Opus 4.5 card that confidently ruling out these thresholds is becoming increasingly difficult (§1.2.4).

cells.question: Q06

passages.quote: we have deployed Claude Opus 4.6 under the AI Safety Level 3 Deployment and Security Standard.
we have prepared a Sabotage Risk Report assessing sabotage-related risks posed by Claude Opus 4.6 and the safeguards we have in place to address them

cells.note: The card ties the ASL-3 Standard to its determination and describes the Sabotage Risk Report as meeting a commitment tied to the AI R&D-4 standard (§1.2.3, §1.2.4.1). A stated safeguard is the developer’s account.

cells.question: Q07

passages.quote: Thus, we judge that Claude Opus 4.6 does not cross the CBRN-4 threshold.

cells.note: Biological evaluations include automated tests, uplift trials and expert red-teaming. The card states that it runs no internal chemical evaluations for the RSP (§8.2.1) and covers radiological and nuclear risk through a government partnership (§8.2.2).

cells.question: Q08

passages.quote: has saturated all of our current cyber evaluations

cells.note: The card reports cyber evaluations, which the model saturated, and a CAISI cyber assessment (§8.4.8), and states that the RSP defines no formal cyber threshold. §8.4 gives a qualitative assessment that the model has meaningfully improved cyber capabilities and ties enhanced safeguards against cyber misuse to it (PDF p. 197); no outcome category or threshold is stated for cyber.

search.read: §1.2.4.3, §8.4 and its subsections

setAside.reason: A qualitative capability assessment with enhanced safeguards tied to it, not a category or threshold under the RSP; given in the note.

setAside.locator: §8.4.8 Assessment by the CAISI, PDF pp. 203–204
setAside.reason: Describes the assessment and vulnerabilities found, without a stated conclusion on risk.

crossFamily.result: minor, applied: the qualitative cyber assessment of §8.4 (PDF p. 197) is given in the note and set aside as not a formal category. Status agrees (open question 3).

cells.question: Q09

passages.quote: Our determination is that Claude Opus 4.6 does not cross either the AI R&D-4 or the CBRN-4 capability threshold.

cells.note: The card qualifies the AI R&D-4 rule-out: the model has roughly reached the benchmark thresholds set for a straightforward rule-out, so the determination rests on a wider judgement (§1.2.4, PDF p. 13), and the card calls the margin to the threshold unclear (§8.3, PDF p. 185).

crossFamily.result: minor, applied: the note keeps the distinction between the benchmark rule-out thresholds and the final judgement, without evaluation-design detail. Status agrees.

passages.locator: §6.1 Introduction and summary of findings, PDF p. 91
passages.quote: attempts to manipulate users toward certain views

cells.note: The card lists attempts to manipulate users toward certain views among the behaviours its alignment assessment looked for. No outcome specific to persuasion or manipulation of people was found.

search.read: Abstract, §1 (including §1.2), §6.1–§6.2, §8.1–§8.5, and a term search of the whole card (about 213 pages)

setAside.reason: Willingness to manipulate or deceive other participants in a multi-agent test environment is reported; the card does not say those participants are people.

cells.question: Q11

passages.quote: Safety evaluations showed Opus 4.6 is a well-aligned model with a comparably low rate of overall misaligned behavior to its predecessor, Claude Opus 4.5.

cells.note: The card reports behavioural audits, sabotage and deception tests, evaluation-awareness and interpretability investigations, and external testing, with conclusions. The abstract notes increases in sabotage concealment capability and overly agentic behaviour in computer use.

passages.quote: We conducted an expert red-teaming evaluation with over a dozen experts

cells.note: Scope: biology (virology and microbiology), more than a dozen domain experts. The card also reports a one-week red-teaming with CAISI (§8.2.4.7) and an external prompt-injection red-teaming benchmark (§5.2.1).

cells.question: Q13

passages.locator: §6.2.7 External testing from Apollo Research, PDF p. 119

passages.quote: pre-deployment testing of Claude Opus 4.6 was conducted by the US Center for AI Standards and Innovation (CAISI) and the UK AI Security Institute (UK AISI).

passages.quote: we have decided to release Claude Opus 4.6 under the ASL-3 Standard
